title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 72
paragraphs: Now for the following reasons Croesus was marching into Cappadocia: first, because he wished to add its land to his own possessions, and then especially because he had confidence in the oracle and wished to take vengeance on Cyrus on behalf of Astyages. For Cyrus, son of Cambyses, had conquered Astyages and was keeping him in captivity; Astyages, who was king of the Medes, was Croesus’s brother-in-law, and he had become Croesus’s brother-in-law in this way. A horde of nomad Scythians, at feud with the rest of their people, withdrew and sought refuge in the land of the Medes. At this time the ruler of the Medes was Cyaxares, son of Phraortes, son of Deioces, who at first dealt kindly with these Scythians, as they were suppliants for his protection. Esteeming them highly, he handed over boys to them to learn their speech and the art of shooting with the bow. Time went by, and the Scythians used to go out continually to hunt and always brought back something, until on one occasion they took nothing, and when they returned with empty hands Cyaxares—who, as he showed on this occasion, was not of an eminently good disposition—treated them very harshly and insulted them. The Scythians, having received such treatment from Cyaxares, considered that they had suffered indignity, and planned to kill and cut up one of the boys who were being instructed among them, and, dressing his flesh as they had been accustomed to dress the flesh of wild animals, to carry it to Cyaxares and give it to him, pretending that it was game taken in hunting. Once they had done so, their plan was to make their way as quickly as possible to Alyattes, son of Sadyattes, at Sardis. This was accordingly done, and Cyaxares together with the guests who ate at his table tasted of that meat. The Scythians, having done this, became suppliants for the protection of Alyattes.
